DN_META: Kashmiri 0.402, Khowar 0.465, Kalasha 0.513, Palula 0.539, Shina 0.560 · 11 lects
DN_BODY:
• Clusters reduce only after intervocalic lenition (reversing costs +0.002 to +0.013, stable across random half-samples), with no gemination or compensatory lengthening: hásta > Shina hāt, karpaṭa > Kashmiri kapur.
  • Kashmiric (Kashmiri, Poguli, Dodi) is marked by c j > ʦ z, which every other lect rejects; Kashmiri and Poguli keep v- where all others have b-.
  • Shina proper (Shina, Ushojo) shares tr > ʦ̣, nasal + stop > nasal and s + stop > stop; Palula, Sauji, Kalkoti and Kundal Shahi share mostly retentions. Shina's innovation-based links go to Khowar (sv > śp, v- > b-, nd > n).
  • Khowar rounding harmony: first-syllable a > o before a following a, u or ō (LOO +0.014), Khowar-only, before length loss. Sauji has its own tr > ɬ, dr > l; Palula an aspiration shift (gōdʰū́ma > gʰōm).
DN_HARMONY: Tested as rules, the rounding before u/ō was adopted (Khowar-only; a closed second syllable blocks it, which fits weight-sensitive stress, but long ō still triggers it), i > e before i was kept but is weak, and an i-umlaut a > e before front vowels in Kalasha and Khowar was rejected: it exists at a 20–25% rate but a categorical rule costs more than it gains.
